channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: Africa holds US$29.5 trillion in minerals, but US$8.6 trillion remains undeveloped as poor infrastructure and fragmented demand block value creation.
item.description: Africa sits on one of the world’s most valuable collections of minerals. According to the Africa Finance Corporation (AFC), the continent holds an estimated US$29.5 trillion in mine-site mineral value, representing about 20% of the global total.

item.title: Russia, Ethiopia trade racks $435 million in coffee and machinery sales
item.description: Trade between Russia and Ethiopia surged to more than $435 million in 2025, nearly tripling from the previous year, underscoring a deepening economic relationship shaped by commodities, agriculture, and emerging technology partnerships.

item.title: Kenya pushes harder to protect its citizens from becoming pawns in Russia’s war
item.description: Kenya has announced its intention to engage the Kremlin regarding the deployment of its citizens in the conflict between Russia and Ukraine.

item.title: Africa's largest diamond producer looks to raise income taxes as diamond boom fades
item.description: Botswana plans to raise corporate and personal income taxes to cushion the impact of falling diamond revenues and narrow a widening budget deficit, according to proposals submitted to parliament this week.

item.title: Russia finally responds to alleged recruitment of Nigerians for Ukraine war
item.description: Russia’s ambassador to Nigeria has rejected claims that Nigerians are being recruited to fight in Ukraine, insisting there is no state-backed programme targeting Nigerian citizens for the conflict.

item.title: With diamond losing its shine, Botswana is set to explore other ‘critical’ options
item.description: Botswana intends to diversify its mining pipeline with the exploration of critical minerals, given a surge in demand juxtaposed with an overload in supply for diamonds.

item.title: U.S. backs major rare earths project in Mozambique, one of southeastern Africa’s largest
item.description: The United States has confirmed its support for the Monte Muambe project in Mozambique, one of southeastern Africa’s largest rare earth developments, as part of efforts to diversify its critical minerals supply chain and reduce reliance on China.

item.title: U.S. to send 200 troops to train Nigerian soldiers as it negotiates for a military base in the country
item.description: The United States is set to deploy 200 troops to Nigeria for military training, as the West African nation, ranked as Africa's fifth most powerful military, faces escalating security challenges.

item.title: Dangote eyes investment in Burundi, committing to investing in Africa alone, and nowhere else
item.description: Aliko Dangote's campaign to extend the reach of his industrial conglomerate across Africa has taken him to the doorsteps of the East African nation of Burundi.

item.title: Zimbabwe plans to extend the president’s rule and shift power from the people to the government
item.description: Zimbabwe's cabinet recently gave its approval to draft legislation that aims to amend the constitution, potentially returning the country's political situation to a familiar, concerning trajectory.
